newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Chevron plans $1.2 billion Asian chemical investments.
newsitem.headline: Chevron plans $1.2 billion Asian chemical investments.

text.p: Oil giant Chevron Corp. is boosting its Asian profile by embarking on a $1.2 billion plan to build its first world-scale petrochemical and petroleum additives plants in the region.

"We are in talks to build a large aromatics project in Thailand," Darry Callahan, senior vice president of Chevron Chemical Co., said at the ground breaking for a $200 million additives, or Oronite, plant in Singapore. Aromatics are hydrocarbons that can be used to make other chemicals such as fuel additives.

Chevron's lubricating oil and fuel additives plant will be its first world-scale plant in Asia, capable of producing more than 100,000 metric tons per year. Chevron Chemical is part of San Francisco-based Chevron Corp.

Callahan said the company was also in talks with the Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) to build a world-scale petrochemical plant, which would use Chevron proprietary technology to produce benzene and paraxylene -- products used to make plastics and textiles.
The total cost of the project would be "in the order of $1 billion," Callahan said, adding that talks were at an initial stage so he was not able to give a date when construction might start.
A typical world-scale plant produces at least 350,000 tons per year of paraxylene and 150,000 tons of benzene.
If built, the plant would be Thailand's second aromatics plant. The first, a 650,000 ton per year plant run by Aromatics (Thailand) Plc, started production in December and is 44 percent owned by PTT.
Callahan said Chevron was keen to build such a plant in Asia and if talks failed in Thailand the company would seek an alternative host country in the region.
Explaining his choice, Callahan said, "The infrastructure and market for the kind of product we are talking about is growing rapidly in the country (Thailand)."
He said Singapore was the company's second choice.
Chevron's other petrochemical investment plan in the region is an $80 million polystyrene plant in China's eastern Jiangsu province.

The company is building a $650 million aromatics plant in Saudi Arabia to produce benzene and cyclohexane. The 50-50 joint venture with Saudi Industrial Venture Capital Group will be completed in mid-1999.
Chevron's Oronite additive plant will be located on an island off southern Singapore and will be completed in late 1998.

"We will be spending in total more than $200 million, which is a very significant investment for the additives industry. Furthermore, the design of this plant is such that we can easily double the capacity when the need arises," Callahan said in a statement.

Chevron said it hoped to raise its share of the $1 billion Asian additive market to 20 percent to 25 percent from the present 15 percent to 20 percent, following the start of the new plant. The Asian additive market is growing at about 8 percent annually, Chevron said.
